rationale: RII residential electricity is Scope 2 grid-supplied energy consumed by homes -> I.1.2.
RII residential fossil-gas is Scope 1 on-site stationary combustion -> I.1.1.
'Other' = non-utility residential heating fuels (fuel oil/propane/wood): Scope 1 -> I.1.1. Medium: RII energy may fold in purchased district heating (Scope 2, I.1.2); not separable.
Commercial/institutional share of RII's combined commercial+industrial+street-lighting electricity -> I.2.2. Medium: bucket spans I.2/I.3; value not split.
Industrial share of the same combined electricity bucket -> I.3.2. Medium: not separable; value not split.
Commercial/institutional share of combined stationary fossil-gas -> I.2.1. Medium: bucket spans I.2/I.3; value not split.
Industrial share of combined stationary fossil-gas -> I.3.1. Medium: not separable; value not split.
Commercial/institutional share of 'Other' non-utility fuels (Scope 1) -> I.2.1. Medium: combined bucket + possible district-energy; value not split.
Industrial share of 'Other' non-utility fuels (Scope 1) -> I.3.1. Medium: same ambiguity; value not split.
RII on-road uses the in-boundary (territorial) method = Scope 1 tailpipe within boundary -> II.1.1. EV electricity (II.1.2) negligible/folded.

City MSW landfill emissions -> GPC III.1. Medium: RII uses methane-commitment (future emissions of this year's waste) vs GPC first-order-decay; values not GPC-conformant; in-city vs exported disposal not split.
City MSW incineration/WTE -> GPC III.3. Medium: RII books WTE in the waste sector; GPC places WTE energy-recovery in Stationary Energy; placement differs.
Recycling carries zero emissions under the US Community Protocol (all-zero placeholder); no GPC source category applies.
